gaps.why: Few countries have such a seasonal mandatory-reporting load on small operators; candidate C-Umrah covers companies only, not hajj service establishments and pilgrim housing/catering subcontractors who must register contracts on state platforms (Nusuk Masar, Motawif).

gaps.category: Food-service and retail municipal compliance: restaurants, cafes, cloud kitchens, groceries (Balady licence renewal, Ghad/Monshaat food safety grading, SFDA inspections, price display, ZATCA)

gaps.why: Restaurants, baqalas and cafes are by far the largest small-operator population in KSA; only worker health certificates (K10) and workshops were looked at, and no food-premises inspection-grade/violation-response workflow was screened.

gaps.category: Small contractor and subcontractor duties under the 2024-2026 Mostadam/Etimad, Mowthaq and 'Musanada' rules (retention, payment registration, labour-camp/housing standards, Wasel/Ejar for staff housing)

gaps.category: Self-employed and freelancer/e-commerce small sellers: Maroof/Commerce registration, e-commerce law obligations, Ministry of Commerce consumer-protection (Mawthooq, e-store registration, returns), social-media ad licence (Mawthooq) and ZATCA marketplace rules

coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K17 (Musaned). No 2026 household-employer rule found; only MHRSD recruitment-office enforcement news.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: No Saudi-specific scrap licensing rule surfaced (results were Omani). Nothing found; unverified whether Balady has a scrap-yard requirement document.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No Saudi pawnbroker or second-hand dealer regime found. Only the commercial pledge registry (Ministry of Commerce), which is for business finance, not pawn shops.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K18. Precious Metals and Gemstones Law needs a Ministry of Commerce licence.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: MOMAH published municipal requirements for tashleeh (deregistered vehicle sale and dismantling centres). Mostly site/capex rules, no recurring register found. Candidate C06.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Camel tagging mandatory (fine up to SAR 10,000 per untagged head), applications through Nama; Anaam platform with 40+ services. Government platforms cover it. Candidate C09.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: MOMAH updated municipal requirements for private abattoirs (date not shown): licence, Civil Defense approval, valid CR. No recurring register found. Candidate C10.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Beekeeper permits for citizens only via Nama/Zira'i with training certificate; individual-level, low money. Candidate C11.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: MEWA fined 42 veterinary establishments SAR 500k; SFDA fined veterinary-preparation establishments over SAR 213,500 for expired licences and expired stock. Candidate C05.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Well licence required (fine to SAR 25k); rig owners need a practice licence (fine SAR 50k to 100k); new Jan 2025 mechanism for farms without deeds via Ihkam. Candidate C07.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: NWC and Elm launched the Tasreeh platform for sewage tankers (Riyadh, Jeddah first) with unified identity and treatment-plant gate access; MEWA licenses non-potable water tankers (fine up to SAR 200k). Candidates C01, C02.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: SASO lift technical regulation mandates periodic inspection by accredited bodies, but I found no official interval or enforcement news. Candidate C08 (unverified).

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Only non-potable water distribution (manahil and tankers) licensing found, covered in C02. Nothing on small drinking-water systems.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Sellers need a licensed practitioner (3-year licence after training) and 2026 pesticide guide published. Two MEWA PDFs too large to fetch. Candidate C12.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K19. MHRSD temporarily stopped new licences for domestic-labour companies (undated Okaz report); Musaned is the incumbent.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Mortuaries (maghasil al-mawta) need a municipal licence and licensed washers with a ministry training permit (Okaz, 28 Sep 2025). Small niche. Candidate C04.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: NCNP governance disclosure phase 2 from Jan 2024 requires annual uploads by all associations; 6,348 non-profits by June 2025; 200+ sanctioned for fundraising breaches. SFDA halal certificate mandatory for importers of five product types. Candidates C03, C13.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Car-rental offices must issue all contracts via the TGA Tajeer unified e-contract on the Naql portal; delivery-app vehicle routing licence rules. Trucking is K16. Candidates C14, C15.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: MOMAH updated itinerant-vendor site requirements (20 Apr 2026) and mobile-cart requirements; SAMA exchange licensing exists but no recurring-report detail found. Candidates C16, C17.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Vehicle repair workshops got a new five-class municipal regime (Sep 2025). Nursery and driving-school searches returned no official Saudi text (unverified). Falcon ownership certificates via Fatri. Tattoo studios: not applicable, no licensed regime found. Candidates C18, C19, C20.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: Energy Ministry guide covers petroleum-activity and LPG licences (retail cylinder sale, wholesale, vending-machine licence). No periodic reporting duty for small retailers found in two searches. Station requalification is K11 and stays rejected. Nothing new beyond K11 apart from weak LPG note.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: GFSA licenses and oversees flour mills and monitors flour distribution to distributors, bakeries and retailers. SFDA licenses food warehouses (fines up to SAR 10m). No small-firm periodic filing found; bakery flour reporting unverified. Coffee and cocoa not searched.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: No cooperative-specific filing found. Non-profit associations have the annual NCNP governance-disclosure upload (phase 2 from Jan 2024) and beneficial-owner disclosure. Listed as a candidate.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: NPHIES claims for clinics is K14. Medical device establishment licence (annual) for distributors found but unverified for optical and dental labs. NRRC radiation licensing for clinics: search returned only foreign results, so unverified.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K07 (RSD). Controlled-drug register and precursor duties were not searched. SFDA MDEL listed as an unverified candidate.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Private civil guard regime: HCIS licences guard firms. The 2025 Interior amendment obliges many small premises to hire licensed guards. Cleaning and manpower subcontracting rules not found. Recruitment offices are K19.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: Contractor classification sits with the housing ministry, and Etimad registration is document-driven. Mandatory 10-year inherent-defects insurance for contractors dates from 2020; its current status is unverified. Engineering-office stage reports are K03 and the LCGPA certificate is K12. Saudization of engineering jobs (30% from 30 Jun 2026) found.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: REGA Fal broker licence now needs the foundational level of the new broker-levels pathway for issue or renewal (Sabq, 19 Jul 2026). A new real-estate advertising regulation reportedly carries fines up to SAR 200k (unconfirmed). The AML search for Saudi DNFBPs returned only UAE material, so the Saudi regime stays unverified.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Hotel Shomoos is K15. Holiday-home hosts need a Ministry of Tourism private hospitality facility permit per unit, plus Ejar registration, and (per a blog only) Shomoos registration. No tourism levy found.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: SFDA food registration and importer rules, SABER shipment certificates mandatory from 1 Jan 2025, and FASAH HS mismatches in Jan 2026. The broker/FASAH angle is K06. Date-export registration returned only policy news. No traceability duty found.

coverage.category: 31. Car rental offices (Tajeer unified e-contract, Transport General Authority)
coverage.found: All rental contracts must be issued through the Tajeer service on the Naql portal. Source figures: 794 establishments and 2,891 branches in 81 cities, with 1.6m individual contracts in Q2 2026. Daftra, RentSyst and RentWorks exist, but Tajeer integration is not confirmed.

coverage.category: 32. Umrah service providers (Ministry of Hajj and Umrah licences, Nusuk)
coverage.found: Five-year licences with criteria on solvency and overstay rates. Fines up to SAR 100k for unlicensed operators. Season calendar for 1448 published. Bank guarantees seized for failures. The Dhamen platform move (Jan 2024 report) is unverified. No vertical software found.

coverage.category: 33. Personal-data protection (PDPL, SDAIA registry)
coverage.found: PDPL fully in force from 14 Sep 2024. SDAIA is building a national controller register on the National Data Governance Platform and circulated a compliance-verification form in 2026. Fines up to SAR 5m. Whether small firms must register is unconfirmed.

coverage.category: 34. Saudization decisions by profession (2026)
coverage.found: Marketing and sales jobs at 60% for firms with 3 or more such staff, applied from 19 Apr 2026 with a SAR 5,500 minimum wage for counting. Engineering jobs at 30% for firms with 5 or more, from 30 Jun 2026 (a minimum wage of SAR 8,000 for counting). Dates conflict across sources.

coverage.category: 35. Inherent-defects (latent defects) insurance for buildings
coverage.found: 2020 municipal ministry decision with four phases and a 10-year policy after the occupancy certificate. No 2026 news, so the current phase is unverified.

coverage.category: 36. Medical device establishment licences (SFDA MDEL)
coverage.found: Compulsory licence for local importers, distributors and makers. Term is 1 year or up to 5 years, and sources conflict. SFDA runs unannounced audits and checks adverse-event reporting and recalls. Coverage of optical shops and dental labs is unconfirmed.

coverage.category: 37. Industrial licences and factory data (Ministry of Industry)
coverage.found: Only monthly ministry statistics (188 new licences in Mar 2026; about 11,700 factories). No small-factory periodic filing duty confirmed.
